contract_plain_english: For every sub-gaussian random variable X, scale X by its own psi_2 norm, square it, exponentiate it, and take expectation; the result is at most 2. The psi_2 norm is the threshold-2 exponential-square scale from Definition 2.5.6. The printed formula does not state how to interpret the zero-norm case.

source_evidence.observation: The source calls X sub-gaussian when it satisfies one of the equivalent properties i-iv of Proposition 2.5.2, and defines ||X||_{psi_2} as inf {t > 0 : E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2}, described as the smallest K4 in property iv.

source_evidence.anchor: Section 2.5 body display adjacent to Equation (2.16): E exp(X^2 / ||X||_{psi_2}^2) <= 2
source_evidence.observation: In the list of bounds that every sub-gaussian random variable X satisfies, the source states the normalized-square exponential-moment inequality E exp(X^2 / ||X||_{psi_2}^2) <= 2.
The defining property (iv) is existence of K4 > 0 such that E exp(X^2/K4^2) <= 2.

binders: X: a sub-gaussian random variable in the source's probability setting.
definitions_and_conventions: The source describes ||X||_{psi_2} equivalently as the smallest admissible K4 in Proposition 2.5.2(iv).
The square applies to X and to the psi_2 norm; the expectation is taken after exponentiation.
hypotheses: X is sub-gaussian, meaning that it satisfies the equivalent properties (i)-(iv) of Proposition 2.5.2.
implicit_context: The claim is one item in the Section 2.5.2 restatement of Proposition 2.5.2 for every sub-gaussian random variable.
The probability space and the standard measurability conventions carried by the term random variable are not rebound in the displayed statement.

details: The random variable is squared before division by ||X||_{psi_2}^2.
The exponential is inside the expectation.
The relation is the non-strict upper bound <=.
The right-hand side is exactly 2, matching both Definition 2.5.6 and Proposition 2.5.2(iv).
The surrounding sentence applies this bound to every sub-gaussian random variable X.
No centering hypothesis E X = 0 is attached to this bound.

undebatable_constraints: The object is the same sub-gaussian random variable X whose psi_2 norm occurs in the denominator.
The conclusion must be E exp(X^2 / ||X||_{psi_2}^2) <= 2, with no replacement of 2 by an unspecified constant.
The psi_2 norm must use the threshold-2 exponential-square definition in Equation (2.13).
The claim has no mean-zero hypothesis.
The inequality is non-strict and points from the expectation to the upper bound 2.
